caption: A small ball of aluminium foil hangs on a thread, and it swings toward a plastic rod that has been rubbed on wool as the rod is brought near.

sa.check: A small ball of aluminium foil hangs on a thread.
A plastic rod is rubbed on wool.
The rod is brought near the ball.
The ball swings toward the rod.
The thread stays taut with the ball at its end.
The rub comes first, then the approach, then the swing.

pc.expect: The ball hangs straight until the rod is close, leans toward it while it is near and hangs straight again when the rod is removed.
pc.fail: The ball swings before the rod is brought near; or stays leaning after the rod has been taken well away; or swings to and fro with the rod held still; or the ball moves while the rod is far off.

pc.expect: The lean is toward the rod: the ball moves to the rod's side of vertical, along the line from ball to rod.
pc.fail: The ball leans away from the rod; or moves at right angles to the line to the rod; or rises straight up; or the rod is drawn to the ball.

pc.expect: The ball hangs from the thread, which stays taut from anchor to ball; the ball does not rise above its anchor.
pc.fail: The thread goes slack while the ball hangs in the air; or the ball rises above its anchor; or the ball floats with the thread curving; or the ball hangs at an angle with no rod near.

pc.expect: The thread is a limp line that stays straight under the ball's weight; the ball is a crumpled foil sphere that keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The thread stands rigid like a rod; or stretches like elastic; or the ball flattens or unfolds; or the ball melts.

pc.expect: One ball on one thread and one rod; the ball stays on the thread; nothing appears, vanishes or passes into the rod.
pc.fail: The ball detaches from the thread and hangs in the air; or a second ball appears; or the ball sinks into the rod; or the thread splits.

pc.expect: The foil's finish, the thread and the rod's colour stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour or size; or the thread changes colour or length; or the rod changes colour.

note: Who holds the rod is not judged.
